body:
As I said above, “in a way that the user can explicitly handle it”, some functionality needs to be added to support this.

The current PR is rather hacky and not so usable since it relies on only item order, and if we are going to go Blender-like, we will need some new way to do it, such as Shift+click to select the leader.

Also probably we should send a proposal for that first, though. https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals

I'm not sure I understand. Blender (and Unity) also seems to work off of which node you select ~~first~~ last as being the leader, which is the way this PR handles it. As for the code, it was done this way because technically the ~~first~~ last node(s) you select may not be Node3Ds for whatever reason, so it finds the first Node3D as opposed to transforms not working at all or doing something invalid.

To explain Blender's selection method, they have only one Active object in the selected objects in addition to the selection state, which can be switched during the selection by Shift+Click. Without the ability to switch it on your PR, it also lacks a clear difference (such as high color saturation) between which is the active or not.

In other words, it should ideally reproduce the behavior of the following video:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92a68cda-5469-4aec-9feb-ba0e77b17aef

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15159a94-fd70-49cb-b7cb-764d2138e38b)

Ok I see and confirmed that at least the shift click functionality does exist in both software.

So, the request then is to add the ability for users to be able to reselect which is the leader node **_while_** multiple nodes have already been selected, and to have the leader clearly identifiable. 

I think the above code is still technically valid for the reason I brought up, but I will look into swapping the selection list order based on shift clicking and having the leader/active node be identifiable.

FYI if you want to modify only the basis, the blender's config should be as follows:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c972e5a-a411-451b-8d9c-6167978ea2f4

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dbfb8381-3ab2-48b8-9c83-e4c9d12425f3)

Understood, although I wasn't explicitly planning to recreate the entirety of all the different options of pivot points in this single PR, I just choose the most intuitive (to me) defaults. I have a personal need for some of these functions and believe the PR in its current state is better than currently what exists in master which is objectively broken per the "before" video in the PR description. 

I agree that at least the shift+click functionality is a necessary quality of life feature to make the rest of this PR desirable though, so I will work on that.

The relative option must be an additional option for local mode. Can you add a button at the top of the viewport that is only visible when local mode is enabled?

It could be a pull-down like in Blender, but since there are currently only two states, one button indicating indivisual or relative local would be sufficient for now. I assume a `"DistractionFree"` icon could be substituted to indicate that indivisual local mode is enabled.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24a8375e-e78a-4bf1-b609-670194ac3f96)

You should support conversion relative to the leader's object space for scale and rotation as well.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d24f14ed-ed53-4b17-9456-5095b1779fff)

The current editor behavior is broken since the gizmo does not rotate in local space, and there is no reference to the axis objects will be moving along. I will take your point that it is still technically the implied default behavior, so I can agree on the compatibility breakage. I will see what I can do.

If you only want to "fix gizmo", you just need to remove the relative-translate behavior shown below since the operation should not be changed.

Otherwise, it is an additional option but as noted there, scale and rotation are still incomplete. Then, if you are going to add the option, this PR should be changed the title to something like: `Added relative-local mode to local mode in addition to indivisual-local when selecting multiple Node3Ds`

I'm happy to look into it, I just typically try to keep the scope of my PRs as small as they need to be, but still useful, since I know the areas of the codebase that I typically touch have a lot of activity. Enhancements like this can take a while to get merged, so I try to make maintenance of rebasing this PR easier for myself and limit the radius of changes that may break functionality, so that it can be easier to revert and debug. 

With that said I'll welcome a different perspective. I'm still learning the ins and outs of working in an open-source environment with such a large software. 😅

I think it would be fine to remove the relative transform behavior from this PR and make this PR dedicated to fixing gizmo with leader highlight. You can send the relative transform addition as a separate PR later.

Just to clarify my position, I agree with the addition of that feature but I just think it should be optional. I have no opinion on changing the default. As long as the user can choose them, relative-local would be fine as the default.

>I think it would be fine to remove the relative transform behavior from this PR and make this PR dedicated to fixing gizmo with leader highlight. 

Agreed, good suggestion.

Yeah, it's just now occurring to me that the current default editor functionality although not entirely functional is still desirable in certain circumstances, which does explain its existence in Blender as you've pointed out. I will save this for a future PR and will only include code that fixes the gizmo and adds the leader functionality as you suggested.

When there is one selection, it is always active. This means it will change the color of the existing gizmo, which is a little concerning.

Insteads, maybe the non active gizmo's saturation should be lowered. Or it would be fine to allow both active and inactive state gizmo colors to be set in EditorSetting.
I do like the idea of having a separate setting for active color, but for now I can make it so the active node highlighting only occurs when more than 1 node is selected. What do you think?
When only one is selected, I think it is okay that it is always active, it is consistent with Blender.
True, well in that case I would not be against adding the active state gizmo color to this PR if that is the path we want to go. I do think it will help this change be less intrusive.

 		</member>

body:
```suggestion
		<member name="editors/3d/active_selection_box_color" type="Color" setter="" getter="">
			The color to use for the active selection box that surrounds selected nodes in the 3D editor viewport. The color's alpha channel influences the selection box's opacity.
			[b]Note:[/b] The “active” means that it is one of the selected objects and is the only one object that can be used as a basis for some operations.
		</member>
```
Since active is a new term in Godot, it would be better to have an explanation of it.
